review_notes: Read the whole target file and the only uses (TorusJets.lean calls primitive_direction_coordinates; planeForm in Moments.lean is ℝ-specific, as is convexHull ℝ on ℝ×ℝ, so the triangle lemmas and eventual_primitive_direction are appropriately real). The sqrt-based final theorem needs ℝ. The one clear generalisation is the purely order-theoretic lemma exists_odd_integer_between. The proof was not compiled, so universe/instance-name details (IsStrictOrderedRing) are untested. primitive_direction_coordinates could in principle be generalised the same way, but that is optional and I did not make it a finding.

findings.excerpt: theorem exists_odd_integer_between (lo hi : ℝ) (hlen : 2 < hi - lo) :
findings.problem: The lemma only uses floor, the field structure and linear arithmetic, yet is stated for ℝ. Nothing about the real numbers (completeness, topology) is used. It also has nothing to do with the later Seshadri geometry, so a reusable fact about floor rings is hidden behind a concrete scalar type.
findings.proposed_change: State it for a linear ordered field with floor: `theorem exists_odd_integer_between {K : Type*} [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K] [FloorRing K] (lo hi : K) (hlen : 2 < hi - lo) : ∃ i : ℤ, Odd i ∧ lo < (i : K) ∧ (i : K) < hi`. The proof is unchanged: take k = ⌊(lo+1)/2⌋, i = 2k+1, use `Int.lt_floor_add_one` and `Int.floor_le` (both stated for a general floor ring), then `push_cast; linarith`, which works over any linear ordered field. The call site at line 64 still elaborates with K = ℝ.
findings.benefit: The lemma becomes usable over ℚ or any floor-ring field, not only ℝ. The statement shows that no real-analytic input is needed. A similar generalisation of primitive_direction_coordinates (needs only Archimedean/floor structure, since exists_nat_pow_near is Archimedean-general) would become possible.

evidence.excerpt: theorem exists_nat_pow_near (hx : 1 ≤ x) (hy : 1 < y) : ∃ n : ℕ, y ^ n ≤ x ∧ x < y ^ (n + 1)
